svg.text: static create(n, p) → Murmur by default
static murmur(): HashStrategy · static fnv(): HashStrategy
private ctor + create() ⇒ caller never sizes m / k by hand ✓
murmur() / fnv() = tiny factory for the Strategy knob
NO interface seam — facade wraps a CONCRETE class
no remove() — you cannot unset a bit (see sticky)
interview entry point — 8 methods, zero surprises
THE CORE — bit array + k probes
bits: BitSet(m) — the whole data structure
elementCount: int — adds seen, NOT distinct keys
synchronized add(e) — set k bits, elementCount++
synchronized mightContain(e) — ANY 0 bit ⇒ false, early exit
mightContain short-circuits on the FIRST clear bit ⇒ fast negatives ✓
ONE monitor lock on every add AND read — no concurrent reads
estimatedFPR() is NOT the formula — it measures ACTUAL fill
upgrade: AtomicLongArray / LongAdder ⇒ lock-free set + test
STRATEGY — where the k positions come from
int hash(String element, int seed, int bitArraySize)
seed = probe index i (0..k-1) ⇒ one interface yields k positions · result MUST be in [0, m)
hash = seed; per char: h = 31*h + c;
NOT real MurmurHash3 — it is 31x + xor-shift
named for the idea, not the algorithm
per char: h ^= c; h *= FNV_PRIME
demo swaps it to show FPR moves
THE MODEL — sizing math lives HERE, not in the filter
ctor validates: n > 0 and 0 < p < 1 ⇒ IllegalArgumentException
both clamped with Math.max(1, ...) so tiny inputs stay legal
immutable + self-validating ⇒ the filter never re-derives m or k ✓
m is an int — > 2³¹ bits needs long + a chunked BitSet
the value object an interviewer will ask you to derive on the board
reads m and k from config at construction (then forgets it)

g.text: add() only ever turns bits ON. So if a key
was added, all k of its bits are still 1:
The reverse is not safe: other keys can
collectively light up all k bits of a key
Hence remove() is impossible: clearing a bit
would break every key sharing it. Need it?
Too few bits per key ⇒ weak evidence,
easy collisions. Too many ⇒ the array
The optimum sits at HALF the bits set:
This impl reports the empirical version of

Probabilistic set membership — BitSet + k probes — LLD
add / mightContain: O(k), independent of n
space: m bits total — NOT the keys themselves
